limitations: Review of laboratory-scale experiments (mL/min to ~2.8 L/min NH3); not directly scalable.
No Sieverts-law expression, pressure exponent, permeance or permeability values are given.
No PSA performance numbers (recovery, purity); PSA only described qualitatively as most developed technology.
Many values read from figures by the review authors (footnote a) or calculated (footnote b).

Internal inconsistencies: Table 3 header labels reaction pressure as 'Permeate pressure'; Cechetto 2021 vacuum H2 recovery 52/80/85% (Table 3) vs 93.5% (Tables 6, 8); Kim 2022 conditions differ between text (472 C, 2840 mL/min, ~1 um) and tables (430 C, 950 mL/min, 5 um); Jo 2018 NH3 method Nessler (text) vs tunable diode laser (Table 10); catalyst utilisation defined per membrane volume but reported in g/cm2.
Source of equilibrium values in Table 3 not stated explicitly (presumably authors' Aspen V11 calculation as in Fig. 2).
relevance: Provides fuel-cell H2 quality constraints (ISO 14687:2019: NH3 <= 0.1 ppm; N2 <= 300 ppm vehicle, <= 50% stationary) for the AmCraX PSA/purification block; equilibrium conversion tables (1, 4, 5 bar; 325-500 C; Aspen V11) as cross-checks for amcrax.thermodynamics and the Aspen RGibbs CRACKER; membrane reactor benchmarks (X > 99%, H2 recovery 90-97.5% at 400-500 C, 4-7 bar) for the separation module's membrane option; qualitative statement that off-gas combustion alone is insufficient to heat the cracker, relevant to the BURNER/heat-integration design. AmCraX PSA recovery 0.85 is not supported numerically by this paper.
